rationale: Each 3x3 block becomes its most common colour including background: three 2s yield 0, while seven 2s yield 2 in demonstration 2.
Each vertical pair becomes 5 if either cell is nonzero: [0,3] yields 5 and [0,0] yields 0 in demonstration 1.
Each 3x3 block returns its most common nonzero colour; the bottom-left block of demonstration 1 returns 1 despite four background cells, and empty blocks return 0.
Each 2x2 block returns its most common colour including 0: demonstration 1 maps two zeros and two 2s to 0, and three 3s to 3.
Each horizontal pair becomes 5 when occupied: demonstration 1 maps [0,1], [3,0], and [2,2] to 5, while [0,0] becomes 0.
Each vertical pair returns its most common nonzero colour: demonstration 3 maps [0,3] and [3,0] to 3, and [0,0] to 0.
Each 2x2 block becomes 5 if any cell is nonzero; demonstration 2 includes a block with one 1 yielding 5 and empty blocks yielding 0.
Each 2x2 block returns its most common nonzero colour: demonstration 1 maps a single 1 amid three zeros to 1 and two 1s with two zeros to 1.
Each 2x3 block returns its most common colour including background: demonstration 3 maps three 1s and three zeros to 0, while six 1s yield 1.
Each horizontal pair returns its most common nonzero colour: demonstration 1 maps [1,0] to 1 and [2,0] to 2, while [0,0] yields 0.
